images.title: Two groups make a factor pair
images.purpose: Show that splitting the primes of 840 into two groups gives a factor and its partner.
images.composition: Six prime tiles sit in two clear groups, a teal group on the left and an amber group on the right, with one equation line centred below and wide margins.
exact_structure: Exactly 6 square prime tiles in total: three tiles 2, one tile 3, one tile 5, one tile 7.
Left group, inside a rounded teal #0072B2 outline: tiles 2, 2, 7; under the group the product 28.
Right group, inside a rounded amber #E69F00 outline: tiles 2, 3, 5; under the group the product 30.
A small reddish purple #CC79A7 × sign sits between the two groups.
One equation line centred at the bottom: 840 = 28 × 30.
rejection: more or fewer than 6 prime tiles, or a count of 2s other than three
the left group not multiplying to 28 or the right group not multiplying to 30
a tile showing a 3 more than once
images.takeaway: Any group of the primes of a number multiplies to a factor, and the primes left over give its partner.
images.description: The primes of 840 split into a teal group 2, 2, 7 making 28 and an amber group 2, 3, 5 making 30, with 840 = 28 × 30 below.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on reading factors from a prime factorisation.
images.teaching_notes: Count the tiles to see that 840 has only one 3, which is why 3 × 3 × 3 cannot be a factor.

image_decisions.why: Grouping the prime tiles shows physically how a factor and its partner come from the primes.
